headline: ASX closed up 1% today while US tech took a hit last night — GOOG and MSFT both down ~2%, but your long-term cases remain intact.

movers.name: Global X AI ETF
movers.note: Strong bounce today as the ASX's AI-focused stocks caught a bid. Despite being down ~10% overall on your investment, today's move shows the theme still has momentum — particularly as AI regulation debates globally keep the sector in the headlines.

movers.name: Alphabet (Google)
movers.note: Fell last night on NASDAQ amid broader tech selling. A TradingKey analysis flagged that Google's free cash flow has dropped even as its cloud division hit $20B — investors are questioning whether heavy AI spending is hurting profitability. Still up ~9.6% overall on your position.

movers.name: Take-Two Interactive
movers.note: Slipped last night along with the broader NASDAQ selloff. No specific company news — this looks like general market weakness dragging gaming stocks down. Your position is about 5% below what you paid, but the long-term GTA VI thesis hasn't changed.

movers.name: Microsoft
movers.note: Pulled back last night with the rest of big tech. Microsoft is highlighted as a top Wall Street AI earnings play heading into reporting season — so this dip may be pre-earnings nerves more than anything structural. Still up nearly 20% overall on your holding.

movers.name: Vanguard Diversified High Growth ETF
movers.note: Solid session today, riding the ASX's 1% gain. This diversified ETF naturally tracks the broad market, so a good day for Australian and global equities lifts it. Still slightly below your entry price overall, but trending in the right direction.

movers.name: Vanguard US Total Market ETF
movers.note: Rose today on the ASX despite US markets falling last night — this is the AUD-hedged lag effect, with today's ASX pricing reflecting prior US sessions. Up nearly 6% overall on your position.

movers.name: BetaShares Diversified All Growth ETF
movers.note: Quiet but positive session today, up just under 1% with the broader ASX. This is a globally diversified fund so it moves with world markets — nothing to be concerned about here.

movers.name: Vanguard Emerging Markets ETF
movers.note: Small gain today. Emerging markets have been buoyed by the slightly stronger Aussie dollar and ongoing optimism around China stimulus. Still marginally below your entry price, but a steady performer long-term.

movers.name: Pilbara Minerals
movers.note: Barely moved today, up just 0.3%. Lithium prices dropped 14% recently after the EU and China struck a hybrid car deal that reduces the long-term demand outlook for lithium batteries. This is a real headwind for PLS — your holding is down 56% overall, and the structural case for lithium is under genuine pressure.

watch_today.title: GOOG: Hold — cash flow concerns, but cloud story intact
watch_today.detail: Google slipped 2.3% last night after analysts flagged that free cash flow (the actual cash the business generates after spending) has dropped despite its cloud division hitting $20B in revenue. The concern is that massive AI investment is eating into profits. For a long-term holder this is worth monitoring, but Google's core business — search, YouTube, cloud — remains dominant. Nothing here changes the multi-year case. Sit tight.

watch_today.title: MSFT: Hold — earnings season coming, expect volatility
watch_today.detail: Microsoft fell 1.9% last night, but is flagged as one of Wall Street's top AI earnings plays heading into reporting season. That means it may be volatile in the near term as results approach, but institutions are bullish on it long-term. You're up ~20% on this one. No reason to change anything.

watch_today.title: PLS.AX: Hold but watch lithium demand closely
watch_today.detail: Lithium prices just dropped 14% after the EU and China agreed on a deal that boosts hybrid (not fully electric) car uptake — hybrids use far less lithium than pure EVs, cutting demand forecasts. This is a structural headwind, not just noise. Pilbara is already down 56% on your position. The investment thesis depends on a lithium price recovery — that's getting harder to see near-term. For now hold, but reassess if the price breaks below $2.80.

watch_today.title: TTWO: Hold — no new bad news, long-term story unchanged
watch_today.detail: Take-Two slipped ~2% last night, but that's just riding the NASDAQ down. There's no company-specific news today. GTA VI remains the most anticipated game release in years and the long-term thesis for TTWO is intact. You're down about 5% overall — that's noise for a buy-and-hold investor. Sit tight.

watch_today.title: Oil pushing toward $99 — watch inflation implications
watch_today.detail: Crude oil (WTI) rose another 1% last night to nearly $99/barrel. The ongoing US-Iran conflict and Houthi activity in the Strait of Hormuz are disrupting global trade routes, keeping oil elevated. Higher oil feeds into inflation, which could delay RBA rate cuts. Worth keeping an eye on for the broader macro picture.

watch_today.title: RBA rate decision hints — unemployment data in focus
watch_today.detail: Australia's unemployment numbers are rising, and markets are watching closely for signals from the RBA (Reserve Bank of Australia) about when interest rates might be cut. Lower rates would generally be good for growth stocks and property. No decision this week, but watch for any RBA commentary.

world.summary: The Middle East remains the dominant global story, with the US-Iran conflict reshaping trade routes and drawing in new players. US domestic politics is heating up ahead of midterms, with Trump reviving election conspiracy theories and blaming aides for dim Republican prospects.

stories.title: US-Iran War Is Upending Two Critical Global Trade Routes
stories.why_it_matters: The ongoing US-Iran conflict is causing serious disruption to two of the world's most important shipping lanes — the Strait of Hormuz and the Red Sea. These routes carry a massive share of global oil, gas and trade goods. Disruption here drives up the cost of shipping and energy, which flows through to higher prices for everyday goods. Oil is already sitting near $99/barrel as a result.

stories.title: UAE and Saudi Arabia Agree to Re-Enter Yemen Conflict Amid Houthi Gains
stories.why_it_matters: The UAE and Saudi Arabia have agreed to jointly re-enter the Yemen conflict after Houthi forces made significant territorial gains. The Houthis, backed by Iran, have been attacking shipping in the Red Sea — a key global trade route. Gulf states re-entering the war risks further escalation across the Middle East, potentially extending the conflict and keeping oil prices elevated.

stories.title: There Is a 'New Normal' of Violence in the Strait of Hormuz
stories.why_it_matters: Experts are warning that military incidents in the Strait of Hormuz — the narrow waterway through which roughly 20% of the world's oil flows — have become dangerously routine. Tanker seizures, drone strikes and naval skirmishes are now happening regularly. This 'new normal' of instability means oil prices could stay elevated for longer, affecting fuel costs and inflation worldwide.

stories.title: Trump Revives 2020 Election Conspiracy Theories as US Midterms Loom
stories.why_it_matters: With the US midterm elections approaching, Trump is again pushing debunked claims about the 2020 election being stolen. Reuters reports he is also blaming his own aides as Republican polling prospects look shaky. The political turbulence is adding uncertainty to US markets — investors hate uncertainty, which partly explains last night's tech selloff on NASDAQ.

stories.title: Trump Administration Threatens California Officials Over Non-Citizen Voting
stories.why_it_matters: The Trump administration has threatened legal action against California state officials, warning of consequences if non-citizens are found to have voted in the upcoming midterms. California and the federal government are in an escalating standoff over election administration — raising the prospect of a major constitutional clash between a large state and the White House heading into the vote.

markets.summary: The ASX had a solid session today, rising 1% to close at 8,806. Last night in the US it was a different story — the NASDAQ dropped 2.15% and the S&P 500 fell 1.09%, as tech stocks sold off on a mix of AI spending concerns and pre-midterm political jitters. Gold ticked up and the Aussie dollar strengthened slightly.

indicators.name: ASX 200
indicators.note: Strong close today, up 1% — one of the better sessions in recent weeks.

indicators.name: S&P 500
indicators.note: Last night's session — fell 1.1% as markets grappled with political uncertainty and tech weakness.

indicators.name: NASDAQ
indicators.note: Last night's session — tech stocks took a real hit, down 2.15%, dragging GOOG, MSFT and TTWO lower.

indicators.name: Crude Oil (WTI)
indicators.note: Nudging closer to $100/barrel as Middle East tensions keep supply concerns elevated.

indicators.name: Gold
indicators.note: Quietly creeping higher — investors parking money in safe havens amid global uncertainty.

indicators.name: AUD/USD
indicators.note: The Aussie dollar gained slightly, now sitting just under 70 US cents. Good for import costs.

politics.summary: Australian attention is turning to the RBA and the jobs market, with rising unemployment numbers prompting speculation about when interest rate cuts might arrive.

stories.title: Eyes on RBA as Unemployment Rises — Rate Cut Hints Sought
stories.why_it_matters: Australia's unemployment rate is ticking up, which typically reduces pressure on the RBA (Reserve Bank of Australia) to keep interest rates high — because a weakening job market means less risk of wages and prices spiralling. Markets are now watching closely for any signal that the RBA might cut rates. A cut would lower mortgage repayments for millions of Australians and generally boost share prices, particularly for growth-oriented investments like the ones in this portfolio.

ai.summary: AI regulation is dominating the AI conversation globally this weekend, with debates erupting in the US and UK about how — and whether — governments can effectively control rapidly advancing AI systems. Meanwhile, the AI chatbot wars are heating up with new model comparisons doing the rounds.

stories.title: Anthropic's AI Safety Bill Has an Alarming Threshold for Government Action
stories.why_it_matters: Anthropic — the company behind Claude AI — has proposed an AI safety bill in the US that critics say sets the bar for government intervention dangerously high. Essentially, regulators could only step in if an AI system poses an almost catastrophic level of risk, which might mean problems are only acted on after serious harm has already occurred. This matters for anyone invested in AI companies (like GOOG and GXAI.AX) — tough regulation could slow deployment, while weak regulation could create systemic risks.

stories.title: California Governor Newsom Boosts AI Regulation Ahead of Possible 2028 Presidential Run
stories.why_it_matters: California Governor Gavin Newsom is pushing for stronger AI regulation in his state, reportedly with one eye on a potential 2028 presidential run. California is home to most of the world's major AI companies including Google, so state-level regulation there can have global impact. Newsom has previously vetoed strict AI safety bills but appears to be shifting his position — which could affect how quickly US tech giants can deploy new AI products.

stories.title: Senior UK Labour Figures Alarmed by AI's Power — and Fear of Being Left Behind
stories.why_it_matters: Senior figures in the UK's Labour government are privately worried about AI on two fronts: first, that it is becoming too powerful too fast; and second, that the government risks falling behind public opinion if it doesn't act quickly enough on regulation. The UK is trying to position itself as a centre for responsible AI development, and internal disagreements about how hard to push regulation could shape the global policy landscape — including standards that Australian companies and ETFs like GXAI.AX would need to comply with.

stories.title: Gemini 4 Argon vs Claude vs GPT-6: What's Actually Different?
stories.why_it_matters: Google's Gemini 4 Argon, Anthropic's Claude and OpenAI's GPT-6 are now the three main AI assistants competing for users and enterprise customers. Roundup comparisons are circulating this weekend, focusing on speed, accuracy and coding ability. For investors in GOOG and GXAI.AX, the AI assistant race matters — it's a key battleground for advertising dollars and cloud computing contracts, which flow directly to Google's bottom line.

sport.summary: The Rugby League World Cup is in full swing, with some big results over the weekend. Tonga pulled off a historic win over England, PNG had a standout day, and there's off-field NRL news around Addo-Carr and the Roosters Grand Final win from earlier this month.

stories.title: Tonga Stun England in Historic Rugby League World Cup Win
stories.why_it_matters: Tonga have beaten England at the Rugby League World Cup — a genuinely historic result. England were considered strong favourites heading into the match, making this one of the biggest upsets of the tournament so far. It's a massive moment for Pacific rugby league and sets up a fascinating group stage.

stories.title: Cowboys Flyer Shines as PNG Secure Big World Cup Win
stories.why_it_matters: Papua New Guinea secured a convincing win at the World Cup, with a North Queensland Cowboys flyer putting in a standout individual performance. PNG are becoming a genuine force in international rugby league — their rising profile is great for the game's growth across the Pacific.

stories.title: Addo-Carr Faces Monster Ban Even With Eels Throwing Lifeline
stories.why_it_matters: Josh Addo-Carr is reportedly facing a massive suspension despite Parramatta Eels reportedly offering him a lifeline contract. The ban could sideline him for a significant portion of next season, making any deal a risky investment for the Eels. A player of his pace and try-scoring ability being off the park is a blow for the competition's entertainment value.

stories.title: AFL: Three-Club Player Retires Immediately at Age 28
stories.why_it_matters: An AFL player who turned out for three clubs has announced his immediate retirement at just 28 years old. The AFL world has paid tribute, with the shock announcement coming out of the blue during what should be the prime years of his career. No further details on the player's identity or reasons were available from the article.
